newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on CBOT, local short covering.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on CBOT, local short covering.

text.p: WCE canola closed higher on support from gains in the CBOT soycomplex and local short covering, traders said.

"Locals covered shorts, there was a lack of commercial orders but rumours of Mexican business on the horizon," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -5.22 Thursday from -5.82 Wednesday. About 135 July-Aug spread at $1, 10 July-Nov $35, five Nov-Jan at $3.90. Volume was 3,225 lots, or 64,500 tonnes, with 100 hedges.
July canola rose $2.90 to settle at $405.90, November up $0.60 to $371.40. July flax lost $0.90 to $330.90 on hedges, November up $0.90 to $316.90 on commercials, 50 July-Nov spread at $15.
July western barley rose $0.50 to $132, October up $0.20 to $133.60 on commission trade. Volume was 400 lots.
July wheat rose $0.40 at $159, October up $0.30 to $160.50 on commercial buying met by hedges. Volume was 123 lots.

Locals bought 35 October feed pea contracts down US$0.20 to US$183.80, commercials bought 45 February down US$1.80 to US$184.20 and five May fell US$2 to US$187 with PCTS the featured seller, a trader said. Oats did not trade.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
